newsitem.title: CHINA: China eyes new beginning in ties with Britain.
newsitem.headline: China eyes new beginning in ties with Britain.

text.p: China said on Tuesday it hoped for a new beginning in its sometimes rocky relationship with Britain after the crown colony of Hong Kong is handed back to Beijing at midnight on June 30.

"We hope China and Britain will strengthen cooperation under a forward-looking spirit so that relations between the two countries could have a new beginning," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told a news briefing.

China's President Jiang Zemin is to meet Prince Charles and Britain's Prime Minister Tony Blair before the midnight handover ceremony in Hong Kong, Cui said, adding that details were still being worked out.

Problems left over from history between China and Britain would be resolved with Hong Kong's handover after more than 150 years of colonial rule, the spokesman said, without identifying those problems. This provided a good opportunity for both countries to develop relations, he said.
China and Britain have been at loggerheads over democratic reforms for Hong Kong.
Cui said it was understandable for some countries to be concerned about Hong Kong's post-colonial future, but it was inappropriate to spread doubts about the enclave's future.
